name: Lake Dumont
summary: Lake Dumont is a secluded, expansive body of water tucked into the rugged mountains of northern Feralas, just north of Dire Maul. Bordering the ridges toward Desolace and Mulgore, the lake hides ancient elven ruins alongside a quiet island marked by a burning tower and an unusual band of castaways.

sections.title: A Hidden Refuge in the Mountains
sections.body: Tucked away high above the canopy of Feralas, Lake Dumont is an immense mountain lake set against the northern ridge separating the wilderness from Desolace and Mulgore. Its northern banks are dotted with crumbled night elf stonework, silent remnants of the ancient civilization that once dominated the region before the Sundering. Isolated from the main roads, the lake remains a quiet, misty retreat seldom visited by travelers passing through the forest below.

sections.title: The Smoldering Island
sections.body: In the center of the lake sits a small island dominated by the smoldering remains of a shattered mage tower. Rubble from the destruction litters both the shoreline and the lake bed, surrounded by an eclectic company of stranded travelers. Despite carrying Alliance affiliations, these castaways—ranging from stargazing observers and resting wanderers to an inter-species dwarf and gnome couple—remain peaceful toward anyone who stumbles upon their refuge, offering a curious pocket of tranquility in an otherwise perilous wilderness.

aliases: how to get to lake dumont
faq.answer: Lake Dumont lies in northern Feralas, high in the mountain ridge directly north of Dire Maul near the border with Desolace.

faq.q: What is on the island in the center of the lake?
faq.answer: The island holds the ruins of a burning tower, a small boat, scattered debris across the shallows, and an encampment of peaceful, stranded travelers.

faq.q: Will the people on the island attack Horde players?
faq.answer: No. Although the castaways appear to be affiliated with the Alliance, they are peaceful and remain friendly to members of both factions.

faq.q: Are there ancient ruins near the lake?
faq.answer: Yes, ancient night elf ruins crumble along the northern shoreline of the lake, near an overland pass leading into the high mountains.

angles.text: The overgrown stonework along the lake's northern shore stands as another forgotten piece of Kalimdor's pre-Sundering past, overlooked beneath the shadow of Eldre'Thalas.
The stranded castaways residing around the ruined tower maintain their friendly disposition despite being cut off far into the untamed Kalimdor wilds.
